## Description

**What**: Implement the defensive guard at check-prereqs phase: parse upstream copier.yml at the pinned commit hash (via `gh api`) and diff required-var list (name + type + accepted-values for enums) against the hardcoded list in strata-template-vars.sh. Fail fast with named error if any copier.yml-required var is NOT in the hardcoded list. At invoke-platform-cli, add hang detector (5s prompt-pattern + 60s no-output) as defense-in-depth.
**Why**: Upstream Strata templates evolve; without a guard we silently miss new required vars and hang on prompts.
**Scope**:
- IN: `gh api` call to fetch copier.yml at pinned commit; YAML parse + required-var diff vs strata-template-vars.sh; named error `[A1] copier.yml required var '<name>' not in --data list; update plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-template-vars.sh`; install-time prompt-pattern detector (5s detection) + no-output detector (60s); kill on detection.
- OUT: nava-platform invocation itself (separate story).

## Done Definitions
- When complete, parse-time test with synthetic upstream copier.yml containing a new required var exits non-zero in <10s with the named error ← Satisfies: SC3
- When complete, install-time test with simulated prompt-pattern in stderr is killed within 5s with the named error class ← Satisfies: SC3
- When complete, no hung script in either path (parse-time or install-time) ← Satisfies: SC3
- When complete, unit tests written and passing for both guard paths

## Considerations
- [Reliability] gh api errors must be distinguishable from copier.yml-divergence; non-200 fails with separate error class
- [Testing] Synthetic copier.yml fixture for the parse-time test must be tracked in tests/fixtures/

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a maintainer, the defensive guard fails fast at parse-time and install-time when upstream Copier vars drift
